- ## SacredSora *—* 2025/4/27 10:22

  first note good. Second note should be something like this to be more specific and allow for a lot of riskiness but smart risky On attack and defense, find more off-angles with your TPs and ways to change up fights, but only after using your Omen kit (scaling, smoking bomb, etc.) and it's "gunfight time." Going solo sewer is bad when you have Skye/Reyna to help, but if Sova is the only one there, I don't mind you taking the 50—just speed up when Sova’s missing. Taking 50s is fine, just know when: delayed dry peeks sewer when the other team makes no noise = bad; initial fights A long for info or damage = good. Off-angle TPs, like height over sewer or midsite on B/C for an initial peek, are good and fine. Dry swinging sewer (and sometimes A long) isn’t the way. Third note Learn to run while smoking, use tps for off angles or scaling onto sites with the team or to initiate it. Supersteve is correct, pay attention to econ to determine your risky play in general. Don't do something just for a funny clip when they are on eco. But still its perfectly fine to do it when you can and all that just... make sure its not when they have shitty guns.

- ## Supersteve1233 [VAL], *—* 2025/4/27 08:29

  15:23 Instead of peeking out wider, you should be going close to the wall and getting ready to swing off your KJ, she has the deeper line and doing so makes sure that you can't be seen from heaven while fighting. 16:37 You know KJ plays C every round, make a plan to break her stuff. Raze nade, skye dog scout, something. 16:42 I assume this was a mistake but TPing on top is hella risky when you know someone's backsite CT. 17:02 You're smoking too deep here, you should be smoking for the next corner, since they have control of the next corner. 18:10 You're letting Reyna solo sewers & ult aggressively against a save. Reyna dies w/o trade bc shes solo, and you die bc that ult was hella risky against a save. This round was winnable if you either went with reyna or called skye to dog sewers. 20:14 Normally wouldn't bring this up but I do feel you might want to go for a TP on an upper area for the surprise factor, be ready to drop down ofc but you haven't done anything like that since round 2 or 3. 20:18 wasted flash, you should be util trading here. They're not pushing you yet. 20:56 you should be telling the team you're smoking it too, that's VERY important for your skye, otherwise she might flash in the smoke/assume false info. 21:47 Not a fan of this smoke, you already have a garage player so you're not really cutting up the site, just giving the enemy team space to play around. It's also sticking out on your side a bit which could be a bit dangerous. Smoking long might be the boring play, but it's the right one. 21:53 Timing aside, you should 100% be saving this for when you found the spike and need to smoke it off. By the time you get to defusing the spike, the first smoke will probably have dropped and now they can't play around it. 23:08 Too greedy lol 24:55 The enemy team is expecting you here because you've already played there twice, you should probably be mixing it up here. General rule of thumb: Once you do it twice in a row, change it up.

  6:17 not that important especially cause u didnt suggest it, but rushing B on a 3 site map is crazy lmao It was really close because its B site, generally pretty bad to hit without A or C link control but even then they have problems 8:16 Once again not a fan of solo here, if you just get skye dog sewers you're chilling 8:50 right here you either need to be running up to your raze to trade them out or holding heaven. - ## Namu [឵឵], *—* 2025/4/3 16:46

  Be careful on crouching, if it happens that much already in DM, you might do even worse in actual games You rarely do A/D movement in fights, and habits like in 1:43 (you crouch despite not even being in a fight) reinforces the pattern While moving, you have often your crosshair in walls, requiring you to make bigger flicks if someone peeks on this timing (2:41-2:49 is biggest example, your aim is very jittery and often end up in the wrong place), working on smoothing it (be more precise on your horizontal placement, less in walls, and if you do the voltaic playlist, the VT x WHJ Smooth Strafe Sphere Easy is nice to reduce vertical jitter) Try to push more the A/D movement even on enemies that don't move / look at you, goal is to make it a habit, you have to see more and more fights that shows "oh, he couldn't hit me because I was schmooving"

- ## Vex_DK *—* 2025/3/28 22:01

  I'm gonna make some guesses, your raw aim seems good but you have no clue where to put your crosshair, so I assume you played some other fps and are lacking hours in valorant dm (if you sent tracker link I could check) 0 min 30 sec (you holding an angle) Your crosshair is way too close to the wall. If you hold an angle your crosshair should be further from the corner compared to what you are doing now, but when you are in an off angle your crosshair should be even further from the corner because the other guy is not expecting you and they are going  accidently wide swing you. If you put your crosshair in the blue spot, if they under swing your crosshair its should be a easy micro flick for you, and if they swing past your crosshair its not as far from it as they would have been if you where looking at the corner, and you chasing them with your crosshair is bad while they line up their shot. 2 min and 38 sec (you peeking an angle) You should only look into the wall when you take a small pause and dedi peek an angle, the small pause is super important. Also your crosshair movement is super choppy here, I don't know if its a sensitivity thing, but it should be a lot more smoother. If a guy was standing there, you should flick a long distance to kill them and if they where moving even further.

- ## jonafanfan *—* 2025/2/1 06:37

  Hey, I watched the VOD, and there's some great stuff here. I love the IGL and comms, but there are a few things we should address.

  1. **No insta-crouching.** Great control of shots with secondary, but ensure that there is no crouching from long rangle with a phantom/vandal.
  2. **Effectiveness of play.** We need to make sure we are not wasting time or wasting bullets when playing around the map. Be faster on your rotates and pushes, no need to hang back, you should be going in second/third after your duelist.
  3. **Control aggressive plays.** As Fade, you need to focus on the objective if you have spike. Don't push too deep, make sure to clear site and plant. Additionally, there shouldn't be any 1v1 peeking in numbers/postplant. Play back on site/with your team.
  4. **Fight with your team more.** You could be a bit more aware of your teammates and their positioning. Try to fight with them, instead of peeking afterwards. Trading is great, but if both of you stay alive, that's even better.

  Other than this, there was not much to say as you played great! Keep it up and you should be able to reach Diamond relatively easily.

- ## jonafanfan *—* 2025/1/28 03:57

  Hey, I watched the VOD, and there's some great stuff here. However, we do need to address some issues:

  1. **Learn how to counter-strafe.** All your 1 on 1 duels were taken with a crouch spray/transfer. You are not going to get past gold if you don't learn how to counter-strafe. Go into the range, or deathmatch and watch some tutorials on how to do this.
  2. **No excessive shifting.** There is no need to be shifting in CT on a site retake, or when rotating, or when pushing up. The only times when you should be shifting is when you are lurking, or in a 1v1. Enemies will already be looking in your direction or rotating, so there is no need to shift. Additionally, stop shifting around angles to clear them. You should only be peeking angles with A and D, no W, no shifting.
  3. **Utility effectiveness.** Please, always put your turret flank on attack, especially on Lotus as it is so easy for flankers to catch you off guard if you have no utility watcing it. And we need to make good use of our ult; you shouldn't be using it when the site is free/you are on a fake. Our ult is one of the most expensive in the game, so make sure it covers as much of enemy territory as possible.

  Other tips: Learn how to jiggle peek properly/jump peek properly especially in 1v1 postplant situations. On defence, play onsite as you need to control site. Play back in main on attack. That's all, good luck ranking up!

- ## jonafanfan *—* 2025/1/26 05:21

  Hey, I had a look at your VOD, and there's some potential here. However, there are a few things we need to address:

  1. **You are playing way too aggressive as an initiator.** Honestly, the way you are aggressively taking space and pushing out it looks like you really should be playing a duelist. However, if you really want to stick with initiator, you need to stop pushing out so fast like this. Play behind your duelist, don't go into site first, and don't aggressively peek angles e.g. mid. You have no utility to escape like Jett or Reyna so you will be punished if you miss your shots.
  2. **Don't rush your utility.** Tejo's utility is very powerful, but you need to stop using it all in the span of 5 seconds. Take your time with the utility, place your missiles effectively, use your stun effectively etc. Our utility doesn't reset at the end of the round, so there is no need to use ultimate in a 4v2, or have your stun out in a 1v1 duel. Your aim is good, so use that to your advantage, don't rely too much on winning your fights through utility.
  3. **Stop lurking.** The whole point of playing initiator is to support your team, mainly your duelists, with utility to get onto site or to control site. If you lurk, all that utility is practically wasted as you can't support your team well. Tejo is an exception, as his utility is usable from afar, but you need to stop lurking and play with your team more as you are losing rounds where you could've traded out your teammates.
  4. **No crouch spray.** I don't want to see any crouch spraying from 50 metres away. This needs to be drilled into your head; no crouching, only strafing.
  5. **Don't overheat.** Sometimes you get a great kill, then you push out even more and die. Once you get a kill, just chill out and play a bit further back. Don't get greedy for more; you just gave your team the advantage, don't lose it again.

  Other small tips: Take spike Don't play into an op, just rotate That's all, good luck ranking up!

- ## frenzy *—* 2025/1/21 00:34

  Sorry I didn't respond, I'm in the UK so it was midnight when you responded. I think if you genuinely don't think someones in going to be on the angle you expose yourself to, then I personally believe you shouldn't look at it at all. And for the inverse, if you think someone is going to be on an angle, be fully prepared and swing like you actually believe it. In deathmatch, you may die doing this a lot since people can just spawn on impossible angles but just shrug it off in that case - "unlucky". Valorant is a game of attention so you should keep your attention honed on where you think a threat is rather than spreading your attention thin even though you don't think someone's there. For example at 1:15 after you kill the Reyna, I would fully hold bottom mid whilst walking backwards towards top mid. Then, after I get to the box at top mid, I would clear it only then. For peaking, you have to think about commitment. A tight peak is very easy to unswing with whilst a wide peak is very exposing.  You also have to think about crosshair placement and your time to shoot. For example, a common strategy is to jiggle tight and shoot some bullets and then take a few steps back and perform a wide swing as the enemies crosshair will be tight. I'm really struggling to explain when to do which peek to be honest but just don't overcommit without info. Pre-aim is placing your crosshair in the wall so it'll be in the correct place when you swing. Tracking is like locking your crosshair to an angle to clear it. Generally: Pre-aim when you have angle disadvantage (angle you're swinging is closer to you than the enemy) Pre-aim when you have info on enemy position Tracking when you have angle advantage (you are further away from the angle than the enemy) I think this video is a good example - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p-p3pH5vIvs

Another alternative is pushing up towards the smoke in order to increase the odds you can right click. You can further increase the odds you live here by crouching to throw off the jett's crosshair placement (if you're jett swinging out of the smoke, you're likely looking towards the right corner at head height, not expecting someone to be crouched hugging the wall close to you). You knew where jett was and there was a much safer route to close the distance rather than you possibly getting one tapped as you peek.round 3: You're reloading and trying to retreat when you sprayed less than half your spectre mag, are out in the open, and heard at least one more mid.   Hey there, some nice gameplay there. I noticed a few major issues you will need to fix to rank up: The main one is PLAY FASTER. Your smokes are hesitant - just pick a place to smoke and stick with it. Rotating? Don't stand and smoke, walk and smoke. Also don't shift for no reason in your half, you should really only be shifting on lurks or in 1v1s.  Another important thing is be CONFIDENT. You're peeking very conservatively and very slowly to clear angles when you don't really have to. Don't be scared of taking a 1v1 or holding an enemy angle. Utility usage - I noticed that you might blind but you won't capatalise on the blind and swing off it. Your blind, when used correctly, is practically a free kill, so just remember that. Don't tp into the open with no information; if you can't see where your tp is going. don't tp. When swinging, swing with your teammates and not one by one, and make sure to have your gun out before swinging and not swinging with your knife out. Your aim is not bad, just minimise spraying from long range Play further back on eco rounds That's all, try and implement this advice into your games. Good luck!

  Round 23:

  - Once again starting the round doing nothing, this time with an op. You need to be peeking something early trying to get an easy first blood and turning the round into a 5v4, every round. You'll never see a radiant jett start backsite B with an op. Usually they're going wide in one of the mains, oping tiles from tree, or oping cat from market, all of which are early potential free op kills.

  Round 24:

  - Second round in a row where you prime dash and don't end up using it. Consider shooting your first op shot without dash and just using smoke to get away from the angle, then using your dash to get out when you KNOW there are enemies. If you saved your dash, then maybe once you got brim smoked you could try a risky play to get one while they walk out main then dash tree.

  Round 25:

  - Why are you hesitating to updraft dash onto site? You've done it confidently before, don't let the odin tell you not to hit that dash this round. Your hesitation costed you here since you got blinded and missed the dash.

  Round 26:

  - Interesting choice to hide behind the box and look at nothing. The least you can do is hold for someone to walk switch. I like the silent jump peek tech but again, staring at the box seems slightly unideal.
  - Instead of dry swinging brim, you could double smoke towards gen to fake him out. Just a suggestion though, and I don't blame you at all for swinging brim, I probably would've done the same

  Congrats on the win, sorry if the notes got slightly lazier as the rounds go on TwT. Overall points:

  - Stop strafing while OPing.
  - Start your rounds productively, be in a position to do something. (this is especially important start of round when EVERYTHING is fair in terms of knowledge)
  - Always be in a position to do something. Always ask yourself "What am I doing to help the team right now" or "what impact am I having". Impact wins rounds, not just kills.
  - Don't use your movement util without intent. Use it to kill an enemy or use it to get away from one, but try not to just use it thinking an enemy *might* be around.

- ## Kiraie [SWAG], *—* 2024/12/23 15:01

  Round 8:

  - poor crosshair placement when you peek cat start of round. I rarely ever see people hold from the right side, and I'm sure many more players choose to hold from the doorway.
  - So by 1:06 you know where roughly 3 are. Jett was spraying B earlier in the round, drone spots cypher and a kj turret. One *could* be market but general point is that 3 are B side. You have 0 clue where Brim is, and it's very possible/likely that he's taken space in a similar manner to your reyna (i.e. he could be holding from top cat or walking through your spawn towards B right now). I appreicate you knowing market/pizza is a threat since reyna passed it and they could have walked through after, but you leave yourself wide open to attacker side cat.
  - If you're gonna dodge kj ult in wine, your clove is 100% right, be careful of the molly play. Classic is way better here than op. You can break kj mollies, and if they push you, you can at least run and gun right click/left click spam.
  - Holy you snapped to that kj behind gen when you saw her arm. Nice adjustment but no need to do that. Just hold and click when they're behind the dot.
  - ^^More specifically, I'm not sure if you've thought about how you hold angles with op. You don't need to jiggle and strafe when holding. By moving you're using more of your brain focusing on pressing keys AND adjusting to the same rough spot every time you move. This could delay your reaction time and your ability to flick to a target. Just hold. The other part is how wide you choose to hold. There's a ton of different factors in how wide to hold, such as your reaction time, whether or not the angle is commonly jump peeked first, what threats the enemy exposes themselves to, etc. I'd recommend either looking at how pros do it or even just consciously thinking about it.

  Round 9:

  - solid round, crosshair placement issues only but aside from that, I don't see anything wrong with the decisions made. I liked how you played time at the end, gj

  -(super nitpicky tho, you jiggled wayy more around the boxes than you needed to, and I'm pretty sure their jett could see your head half that time, esp with jett's model having a ponytail)

  - one big strength of jett knives is the ability to be fully accurate while moving, why not jump around the corner instead of running to make yourself a harder target? unless you don't trust your aim, in which case learn to trust it, you'd be surprised :)
  - your planting sova is not going to turn and kill you, there is no need to put your crosshair on him here, it's okay, they're your teammate /s
  - after killing kj, this phoenix knows EXACTLY where you are and you have no clue where they are, huge disadantage for you. At this point, phoenix is either heaven or tree. You got your sova's tree, sova's got your heaven, neither of you can get shot in the back and you're both chilling. ++ when phx sees sova gen his crosshair will move there, that's the most free kill of your life

  round 7: 

  - nothing particularly wrong with this round imo. My advice is instead of thinking "what should I do next" you should focus more on "what am I doing right now and is it helping the team". - ## ION Prod. [DOJO], *—* 2024/12/13 21:07

  ----------------- And specifically on jett, entry isn't quite as hard as you might think. I'm not super advanced into it but the general strategy is throw a cloudburst into the middle of the site (but close enough that you can dash to it) and dash into it right after it forms. From there you want to figure out if you saw anyone when you went in, then check your minimap briefly to see if your team is walking in or if they see someone. If your team is out and you see someone on minimap you can fight then you preaim and peek to fight them. If you get hit with some util or your team is still not out you can smoke yourself again. The main difficult thing is just doing this all in under 5 seconds

- ## RafiTheLegend *—* 2024/12/10 04:30

  Micro -

  1. Communication is VERY little. You didn't comm a lot until round 22.

  -Defense: There were times you pushed on attack that you had control of A main, but never commed. you took space. you could have held and wait to see if something happens mid or B. 

  - Defense: dry peeking mid without utilizing cloves smokes to take space. you kept getting timed.

  

  - Attack: being the 3rd or 4th one into site. one of the best advantages of reyna is she can dismiss. need to have confidence on your ability to push in. or ask flash from initiator to entry in.

  

  1. Aim - Slicing the pie or holding off angle needs a bit more work. ties back to utilizing smoke from clove.

  

  1. playing off angles like a phoenix to maximize your play potential. there were moments where you were holding flower out in the open, so they swung you and got you easily.

  Macro - 

  1. Map awareness is not great. need to identify where team is and think "what would i do if i was on attack". there were rounds where they got around you easily or got timed or pushed further you needed to.

  

  1. first half you looked like you were autopiloting

  

  1. learning post plant for reyna relative to team (this comes with trial and error). you need to build confidence on your duelist roll to take space, but to not overheat.

  That was a close game at the end! Great come back! Personally. you made great improvement if you look at your performance over all acts! continue to work on your aim, but i would focus more on positioning, cause your aim itself is good and isolating angles (slicing the pie).  I hope these help!!

- ## Mang Tomas *—* 2024/11/29 02:22

  Your aim looks pretty good for gold/plat but if you want to be able to solo carry in your ranked games you have to practice how you would peek/play in a ranked game. What I like to do in dms is to pretend I'm in a 1v5 and methodically clear my way to a site which translates very well in my ranked games. Also for the strafes, if you look at zekken, demon1, florescent, you can almost never see them do those kinds of strafes which just messes up your aim which is clearly visible because when you do not do those strafes, you can actually hit people. Instead of just doing those strafes, you can think of the strafing movement as a way to reset your aim when you do whiff so that your strafing actually gives you a bit more time to aim.
